_comment: no-graphql-without-adr gate policy (DATA, not code). ADR-0565 (founder 2026-06-21, door: one-way) removes ALL GraphQL from the owned API surface: the canonical surface set is REST + gRPC + AsyncAPI + realtime (SSE / WebSocket / gRPC-streaming). GraphQL is admissible ONLY via a future ADR that explicitly reverses ADR-0565. This gate is the enforcement half (the drop PR #775 is the construction): it fails CLOSED if the candidate tree reintroduces a GraphQL execution/parse library (in ANY Cargo.toml dependency table in the tree — members AND non-members, resolving [workspace.dependencies] renames and {workspace=true} inheritance), a forbidden GraphQL crate in the resolved Cargo.lock graph (the transitive catch), or a .graphql/.graphqls/.gql/.gqls/.sdl schema file, in EVERY case WITHOUT the artifact citing an ALLOWLISTED + VALIDATED authorizing (reversing) ADR id. The escape-hatch is gated on the authorizing_adrs allowlist (EMPTY today) INTERSECTED with docs/decisions validation (Accepted ADR that reverses ADR-0565), so a bare/fabricated/typo ADR token cannot launder. CANDIDATE-TREE EVALUATION, NOT a frozen merge-base: the gate scans the live tree manifests + Cargo.lock + a read-only file walk, so the verdict is identical at PR-tier and push-tier (avoiding the gate-baseline PR/push asymmetry false-green). FROZEN BASELINE = EMPTY (the tree is GraphQL-free post-drop). ALL repo-specifics are DATA here: a different repo adopts the gate by repointing forbidden_crates / schema_extensions / forbidding_adr / authorizing_adrs / decisions_dir / excluded_dirs.

forbidden_crates.reason: async-graphql + its siblings (async-graphql-actix-web, async-graphql-axum, async-graphql-warp, async-graphql-value, …) are a GraphQL execution/server runtime; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL in the owned stack.
underscore spelling of the async-graphql family.
juniper + juniper_* are a GraphQL server runtime; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.
graphql-parser is a GraphQL query/schema parser; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.
graphql-client + graphql_client_codegen are a GraphQL client/codegen; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.
cynic + cynic-codegen are a GraphQL client; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.
apollo-router, apollo-compiler, apollo-parser, apollo-federation, … are GraphQL gateway/parser/federation libraries; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL (no BFF/federation carve-out).
gql_client is a GraphQL client; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.
GraphQL introspection-query helper; ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL.

product_contract.candidate_tree_not_frozen_baseline: The gate scans the CANDIDATE tree (EVERY Cargo.toml in the tree + the resolved Cargo.lock graph + a read-only .graphql/.graphqls/.gql/.gqls/.sdl walk), NOT a frozen merge-base baseline. A frozen-baseline predicate evaluated at PR-tier against the merge-base but at push-tier against the integrated tip is the PR/push baseline-asymmetry false-green (gate-baseline-pr-push-asymmetry memo): a GraphQL artifact added on dev between branch-point and merge would pass PR-tier and only fail on the integrated tip. Candidate-tree evaluation makes the verdict identical at both tiers.
product_contract.frozen_baseline_empty: The drop PR (#775 / ADR-0565) leaves the tree GraphQL-free, so this gate ships born-blocking with an EMPTY baseline: no shrink-only legacy debt. Any NEW GraphQL library or schema file fails closed on arrival.
product_contract.adr_escape_hatch: ADR-0565 admits GraphQL ONLY via a future ADR that explicitly reverses it. A forbidden artifact is laundered iff it cites an ADR id that is BOTH (1) enumerated in the authorizing_adrs ALLOWLIST below (EMPTY today — nothing authorizes GraphQL, so an arbitrary/fabricated/typo id like ADR-9999 or ADR-05650 CANNOT launder) AND (2) validated against the real tree: the id resolves to a docs/decisions/ADR-<id>-*.md whose frontmatter status is Accepted and that supersedes/reverses forbidding_adr. The cited id is always a DIFFERENT ADR than the forbidding one, so a file can never self-launder by merely mentioning ADR-0565 (the rule it would be violating). The escape is construction-over-flag: a real reversal is a reviewed Accepted ADR PLUS a reviewed allowlist edit, both validated by the gate — not a bare suppression comment.
product_contract.authorizing_adrs_contract: authorizing_adrs is the CLOSED set of ADR ids that may launder a forbidden GraphQL artifact. It is EMPTY today (ADR-0565 forbids GraphQL with no current reversal). To reintroduce GraphQL, an ADR that reverses ADR-0565 must first be Accepted in docs/decisions, then its id added here in the SAME reviewed change; only then can a Cargo.toml / schema file cite it. The gate intersects this allowlist with docs/decisions validation, so an allowlisted id that is not actually an Accepted reversing ADR still does NOT launder (defense in depth).
product_contract.pack_shaped: forbidden_crates (exact + prefix), schema_extensions, forbidding_adr, authorizing_adrs, decisions_dir, excluded_dirs, and min_expected_workspace_members are DATA; the Rust engine hardcodes no crate name nor ADR id. A different repo adopts the gate by repointing this policy.
product_contract.fail_closed: A member-resolution error, an unreadable candidate tree, a policy gate_id mismatch, a malformed forbidden/extension list, or a too-small member census all fail CLOSED rather than silently passing as a false-green. The escape-hatch also fails closed: an empty allowlist, a missing docs/decisions ADR, a non-Accepted (Proposed/Draft/template) ADR, or an ADR that does not actually reverse forbidding_adr all decline to launder.
product_contract.lock_transitive_catch: The resolved Cargo.lock graph is scanned for forbidden crate names so a GraphQL crate pulled in transitively (named by no manifest directly) still fails closed (NGQL-LOCK-FORBIDDEN). KNOWN LIMITATION: an inline-SDL string literal / derive macro with NO schema file is not caught by the schema-file walk, but any real GraphQL server needs a GraphQL library, which the manifest legs + this lock leg DO catch.
product_contract.hermetic: The collector is read-only fs over the candidate tree (workspace members via oya-workspace-members-kernel for the census floor; a recursive Cargo.toml walk for the LIB leg; the root [workspace.dependencies] table; the Cargo.lock graph; docs/decisions for ADR validation; a recursive schema-file walk). No cargo/buck shell-out, no shell, no network, no VCS — runnable in any presubmit.

purpose: no-graphql-without-adr gate. Mechanically ENFORCES the ADR-0565 zero-GraphQL doctrine: no GraphQL execution/parse library and no .graphql/.gql/.sdl schema file may enter the candidate tree without referencing an authorizing (reversing) ADR. The canonical owned API surface is REST + gRPC + AsyncAPI + realtime.
